entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Rahul Saxena, Advocate holding brief of Sri Manish Joshi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.782 of 2020, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C.,
Police Station Puwayan, District Shahjahanpur, during the pendency of trial.
Suresh vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37983641/
1 4.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the case of the applicant is at better footing to co-accused person Lalaram, who has already been enlarged on bail by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 28.7.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.24223 of 2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.24223 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 19.9.2023.

He further submitted that since the role of the applicant is identical to that of co-accused who has already been enlarged on bail, he is also entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.
5.
The prayer for bail has been vehemently opposed by learned A.G.A.
However, the aforesaid factual aspect of the parity to the co-accused has not been disputed by him.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial and in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938 and the judgement passed by the Apex Court in Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director, Central Bureau of Investigation,
MANU/SCOR/22410/2021, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director, Central Bureau of Investigation,
MANU/SCOR/22410/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed on the ground of parity.

7. Let the applicant- Suresh, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
8. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

9. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
